topics.label: Introduction and lecture learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the framing for the lecture, introducing the lecturer, the course context, and the primary learning outcomes.

topics.label: Foundations of cancer causation: genetics, environment, and epidemiology
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics introduce the fundamental principles of cancer etiology, exploring how endogenous mutations, inherited genetic predispositions, environmental exposures, and geographic variations collectively influence cancer risk.

topics.label: Oncogenic pathogens and the etiology of Burkitt lymphoma
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how infectious biological agents contribute to oncogenesis, using the epidemiological and molecular mechanisms of Burkitt lymphoma as a primary case study.

topics.label: Chemical and physical carcinogens, metabolic activation, and tumor promotion
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail how specific chemical and physical carcinogens induce DNA damage, undergo metabolic activation, or function as non-mutagenic tumor promoters under distinct physiological conditions.

topics.label: Methodologies for identifying carcinogens and evaluating exposure risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the experimental, sequencing, and epidemiological methods used to determine carcinogenicity, concluding with the practical evaluation of carcinogen risks versus benefits.

topics.label: Lecture summary and conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides closing framing, summarizing the main takeaways of the lecture before concluding.
